title: Bench aggregator and regression detection for kernel-swap telemetry
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an aggregator and regression-detection pipeline that consolidates golden-run outputs across kernel variants and prefill/decode scheduling permutations. The goal is to reduce noise in CI perf gates while increasing sensitivity to meaningful regressions introduced by kernel swaps, attention optimizations, or prefill scheduling changes. Deliverables: 1) bench-aggregator service to normalize and merge run artifacts, 2) a detection engine that flags statistically significant regressions using percentile-based and change-point techniques, 3) CI integration that gates merges with a staged canary and async heavy-suite runs, and 4) dashboards and automated ticketing for triage.
acceptance_criteria: Aggregator normalizes input runs from at least 3 kernel variants and outputs deterministic summary artifacts (JSON) with per-cohort percentiles
Regression detector flags >75th percentile increases in p95 latency with fewer than 10% false positives on historical runs
CI pipeline blocks merges when a direct code change causes a confirmed regression; provides a canary path that allows safe rollouts
Console dashboard shows diff heatmaps for attention-related metrics, KV cache hit ratios, and micro-batch distribution
Automated regression tickets are created with links to the golden artifacts, failing CI logs, and suggested suspect commits
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed — validated that historical runs (last 12 weeks) include kernel tags and sample-level seed metadata needed for aggregation.
2026-03-04: Prototype aggregator implemented (Python) that ingests run artifacts from S3, normalizes tokenization differences, and computes cohort percentiles.
2026-03-06: Ran pilot across 120 golden runs; observed high variance in short-sequence decode p95 when prefill batching changed — added warmup-seed normalization to reduce noise.
2026-03-08: Naive z-score detector produced excessive false positives; switched to a hybrid approach with Bayesian change-point detection + percentile gating.
2026-03-10: CI integration PR opened (github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4821) which wires the aggregator into the merge-check workflow. Awaiting review from infra team.
decisions: Use S3 bucket tagged 'bench-golden' for storing normalized artifacts and lockfile references (decision: avoids DB migration and simplifies reproducibility).
Detection algorithm: hybrid percentile gating (p95/p99) + Bayesian change-point to minimize flakiness while preserving sensitivity to real regressions.
Canary strategy: on merge, run lightweight fast-suite in primary CI; if flagged, block merge and schedule heavy-suite async in a dedicated runner with longer timeout and deterministic seeds.
Add lightweight sample-level telemetry fields (kernel_id, attention_fallback_count, kv_cache_hit_ratio, micro_batch_size) to all bench runs to improve attribution.
risks: Compute cost: heavy-suite async runs may add significant CI spend if many merges trigger them — mitigation: rate-limit heavy-suite and prioritize PRs by risk score.
Upstream telemetry gaps: some older golden artifacts lack kernel tags — mitigation: backfill where possible and ignore incomplete runs in baseline computation.
False negatives: subtle quality regressions that don't show in latency percentiles could slip through — mitigation: add quality/eval checks as complementary gates.
Complexity: increased pipeline complexity may slow down developer feedback loop — mitigation: surface fast, actionable summaries and keep blocking thresholds conservative.
implementation_steps: 1) Schema: design normalized artifact schema (cohort, seq_len_bucket, kernel_variant, seed_hash, metrics) and publish spec in Confluence.
2) Aggregator service: implement ingestion, normalization, and deterministic summary generation. Unit tests for tokenization/seed alignment.
3) Detection engine: implement hybrid detector with config-driven thresholds and guardrails for low-sample cohorts.
4) CI integration: add merge-check that runs fast-suite and calls detector; hook to create an incident-style ticket when heavy-suite required.
5) Dashboard: surface diffs and heatmaps in Console with direct links to S3 artifacts and failing PRs.
6) Runbook: document triage steps, thresholds for accepting rollouts, and rollback guidance for kernel regressions.
notes_for_review: Benchmark normalization must be idempotent — reviewers: please validate tokenization alignment strategy in the spec.
Detector tuning knobs are in config/detector.yaml; CI integration includes a feature flag to disable blocking during ramp-up.
